summary: This note is a wiki-style biography of Max Huber, a Swiss legal scholar and statesman. It covers his legal education, his teaching post at the University of Zurich, and his wartime advisory role. It then summarizes his long international service as a judge and president of the Permanent Court of International Justice, his presidency of the International Committee of the Red Cross, and his arbitration of the Island of Palmas Case.
one_line: Biography of Swiss jurist Max Huber, who served on the Permanent Court of International Justice and led the International Committee of the Red Cross.
key_facts: Max Huber studied law at the Universities of Lausanne, Zurich and Berlin.
Max Huber taught international, constitutional and canon law at the University of Zurich from 1902 to 1914.
Max Huber kept his University of Zurich title until 1921 but could not teach because of World War I.
During World War I, Max Huber advised the Swiss Defence and Foreign Affairs ministries.
Max Huber was a Judge of the Permanent Court of International Justice from 1922 to 1939.
Max Huber served as President of the Permanent Court of International Justice from 1925 to 1927.
Max Huber was president of the International Committee of the Red Cross from 1928 to 1944.
Max Huber acted as arbitrator in the Island of Palmas Case between the United States and the Netherlands in 1928.
The Island of Palmas Case was heard at the Permanent Court of Arbitration.
